intro.heroCopy: Each vignette summarizes the early years and warning signs of a real person without giving away their name. Your call: will they escalate all the way to murder?
howSteps: Review the key facts: family, behaviors, first offenses.
Decide in a tap whether this individual will carry out murder.
Reveal their identity and compare your instinct to the documented outcome.
intro.goalCopy: Measure your biases and convictions across a series of contrasting profiles. The final score sums up your predictions and opens up discussion prompts.

p01.label: Profile 01
p01.summary: Thrown out of her home as a teen, she survived by hitchhiking and sex work along U.S. 1, collecting a thick arrest file for disorderly conduct and theft.
highlights: Neighbors remembered her target practice with a .22 pistol in the woods behind budget motels.
Regularly stole clients' cars and dumped them hours later, leaving purses and IDs in dumpsters.
Told her girlfriend she 'hated' johns and fantasized about wiping them out.

reveal.verdict: Confessed to killing seven men while posing as a stranded hitchhiker; executed in 2002.
reveal.detail: Investigators tied her to abandoned vehicles, spent shells, and pawn slips from victims' belongings.

p02.label: Profile 02
p02.tagline: Puzzle-obsessed clerk keeps a private tally
p02.summary: A supermarket stocker who bragged to classmates that life was a giant chess match and that he intended to 'fill the board' before retirement.
highlights: Told friends he wanted one victim for each of the 64 squares on his beloved chessboard.
Invited coworkers to drink vodka in Bittsevsky Park, then bludgeoned them with a hammer and dropped them down wells.
Recorded himself torturing stray dogs, keeping the tapes as rehearsal material.

reveal.verdict: Convicted in 2007 of murdering 48 people, though he claimed 60-plus victims.
reveal.detail: Police matched his victims to the chessboard tally he kept under his floorboards.

p03.label: Profile 03
p03.tagline: Engineering brilliance consumed by germ fears
p03.summary: An heir who built movie studios and aircraft companies, then retreated behind blackout curtains and dictations delivered via Kleenex-wrapped pencils.
highlights: Locked himself inside a screening room for months, living on milk and chocolate bars while giving hourly memos.
Ordered aides to burn clothing he believed contaminated and insisted on surgical masks during every interaction.
Spent millions on experimental aircraft like the H-4 Hercules despite multiple near-fatal crashes.

reveal.verdict: Eccentric billionaire aviator whose paranoia never escalated into homicide.
reveal.detail: Remembered for aviation records, hospital donations, and founding Hughes Medical Institute.

p04.label: Profile 04
p04.era: Washington State & Utah, United States - mid 1970s
p04.summary: A scholarship student who volunteered for political campaigns and manned a suicide hotline while hiding escalating fantasies of domination.
highlights: Collected plaster arm casts and feigned injuries to lure women toward his Volkswagen Beetle.
Visited crime scenes posing as an investigator to eavesdrop on detectives.
Escaped custody twice in 1977 and resumed roaming road trips without alerting family.

reveal.verdict: Convicted of multiple murders in Florida and linked to at least 30 killings across the United States.
reveal.detail: Executed in 1989 after eyewitness testimony, bite-mark analysis, and forensic fiber matches.

p05.label: Profile 05
p05.era: Washington, D.C. & New York, United States - 1930s to 1950s
p05.summary: A patrician-born organizer who transformed the ceremonial role of First Lady into a relentless campaign for workers, women, and refugees.
highlights: Held women-only press conferences that forced newspapers to hire female reporters.
Visited coal mines, prisons, and segregated hospitals despite threats from segregationists.
Chaired the UN committee that drafted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

reveal.verdict: Social reformer and diplomat; no involvement in violent crime.
reveal.detail: Used her platform to expand civil rights and humanitarian corridors during WWII.

p06.label: Profile 06
p06.summary: A respected general practitioner celebrated for punctual bedside visits who kept unusually tight control over medical records and cremation paperwork.
highlights: Patients died minutes after routine morphine injections he administered without charting symptoms.
Forged Kathleen Grundy's will to make himself sole beneficiary of her estate.
Had already been disciplined in 1975 for falsifying pethidine prescriptions to feed his own addiction.

reveal.verdict: Found guilty of murdering 15 patients, with an inquiry later attributing more than 200 deaths to his practice.
reveal.detail: Received 15 life sentences in 2000 after statistical audits of death certificates exposed the pattern.

p07.label: Profile 07
p07.summary: A young dancer who carried resistance messages during the Nazi occupation before becoming a film star and global humanitarian.
highlights: Survived the Dutch Hunger Winter, secretly raising funds with 'blackout' dance recitals.
Abandoned a professional ballet career after war injuries but redirected discipline into acting.
Spent her final decades as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador visiting famine zones in Africa and Asia.

reveal.verdict: Oscar-winning actor and humanitarian; never associated with violent crime.
reveal.detail: Remembered for 'Roman Holiday,' 'Breakfast at Tiffany's,' and hands-on relief missions.

p08.label: Profile 08
p08.summary: A polyglot who hopped between Bangkok, Kathmandu, and Bombay selling fake gems while cultivating a rotating coterie of adoring travelers.
highlights: Used stolen passports to reinvent himself as a wealthy dealer and lure victims to private villas.
Drugged guests with pills he said cured dysentery, leaving them incapacitated for robbery or worse.
Escaped Tihar Prison in 1986 by drugging guards with a farewell cake and walking out the gate.

reveal.verdict: Linked to at least a dozen murders of backpackers across Thailand, Nepal, and India.
reveal.detail: Earned the moniker 'Bikini Killer' and is serving a life sentence in Nepal after a 2003 arrest.

p09.label: Profile 09
p09.tagline: Educator storms Capitol Hill with only volunteers
p09.summary: A headstrong teacher who opened day-care centers before running for Congress on a pledge to challenge both parties' power brokers.
highlights: Refused corporate donations, relying on church basements and schoolteachers for small-dollar support.
Pushed child-nutrition and minimum-wage bills while receiving racist threats and heckling.
Announced a 1972 presidential bid to force civil-rights planks into televised debates.

reveal.verdict: First Black congresswoman in the United States; trailblazer without violent offenses.
reveal.detail: Her 'Unbought and Unbossed' platform inspired later generations of public servants.

p10.label: Profile 10
p10.tagline: Basement odors brushed off as bad plumbing
p10.summary: A solitary chocolate factory worker who paid rent on time and offered beers to neighbors, even as police fielded repeated nuisance calls about his apartment.
highlights: Tenants alerted management to rancid smells, buzzing saws, and dark liquid leaking from vents.
Previously convicted of molesting a 13-year-old boy; still received early release and minimal supervision.
Told childhood friends he liked collecting roadkill and bleaching bones in acid jars.

reveal.verdict: Confessed to murdering and dismembering 17 men and boys between 1978 and 1991.
reveal.detail: Police recovered body parts, photographs, and written plans for more killings inside his apartment.

p11.label: Profile 11
p11.summary: A lawyer who co-founded an armed wing against apartheid, studied Afrikaans in prison, and later negotiated elections instead of revenge.
highlights: Helped organize Umkhonto we Sizwe sabotage cells targeting infrastructure rather than civilians.
Spent 27 years incarcerated on Robben Island, reading law textbooks and mediating inmate disputes.
After release, championed a Truth and Reconciliation Commission instead of purges.

reveal.verdict: Led South Africa into multiracial democracy and received the Nobel Peace Prize.
reveal.detail: Advocated reconciliation and never faced homicide allegations despite militant training.

p12.label: Profile 12
p12.tagline: Personas multiply with every album cycle
p12.summary: A restless performer who reinvented himself with alien alter egos, occult reading binges, and meticulously choreographed stagecraft.
highlights: Isolated for weeks to fast and storyboard characters like Ziggy Stardust and the Thin White Duke.
Immersed himself in surveillance imagery and Expressionist art during the Berlin Trilogy years.
Collaborated with mime artists, fashion designers, and film directors to keep audiences unsettled.

reveal.verdict: Genre-defying musician with zero record of violent crime.
reveal.detail: Left a catalog of innovation and philanthropic support for HIV/AIDS causes.
